units.passage: Most journals and publishers do not permit AI tools to be listed as authors because AI cannot take responsibility for the work. Disclosure of AI use in methods or acknowledgments, when applicable, is typically the appropriate approach.
units.why: "Most journals and publishers do not permit AI tools to be listed as authors because AI cannot take responsibility for the work." AI is not an author, P96.

units.passage: While major publishing organizations such as the Committee on Publishing Ethics have clearly stated generative AI tools can not be listed as authors on papers, it is important that scholars at all levels be transparent about their use of these tools.
units.policy: Major publishing organizations have stated that generative AI tools cannot be listed as authors on papers.
units.why: "generative AI tools can not be listed as authors on papers" says AI cannot be an author, matching P96.
units.fit_note: Reports publishers' position and pairs it with a transparency expectation.

units.passage: Three common citation guides—APA, MLA, and Chicago—all agree that LLMs are not au- thors and therefore cannot be cited as human authors
units.why: APA, MLA and Chicago agree "LLMs are not authors and therefore cannot be cited as human authors": AI is not an author, P96.
units.fit_note: Combined with the statement that LLMs still need acknowledgment.

units.passage: The general consensus among prominent scien- tific publishing organizations is that AI models can- not be credited as authors because they cannot be held accountable for their statements.
units.why: AI models "cannot be credited as authors because they cannot be held accountable": AI is not an author, P96.

units.passage: However, it is crucial to recognize that these tools mimic, rather than replace or even imitate, human creative, technical, and scholarly endeavors. They are not original or creative; they do not have analytical or critical capacities; and they are not driven by curiosity or human agency.
units.why: Claims the tools "mimic, rather than replace or even imitate" human work and "do not have analytical or critical capacities"; a rationale about what AI is, nearest P96 (AI is not a person or author) though it is not about authorship rules, hence fit_note.
units.fit_note: Argues AI lacks creativity and critical capacity rather than saying it cannot be an author, source or collaborator. / Argues AI lacks creativity and critical capacity; it does not say AI cannot be an author or source.

units.passage: AI tools cannot be listed as authors of scholarly work
units.why: "AI tools cannot be listed as authors of scholarly work" says AI cannot be an author, P96.
units.fit_note: Reasons given are responsibility, conflict of interest and copyright, not collaboration.

units.passage: Note that AI will not be considered a “scholarly source” for assignments requiring specific types of references.
units.why: "be considered a scholarly source for assignments" says AI is not a citable scholarly source (P96).
units.fit_note: Says AI is not a scholarly source for reference requirements; does not say it cannot be an author or collaborator.

units.passage: However, the use of generative AI tools crosses the boundary of acceptable collaboration and is not conducive to your academic growth.
units.why: CENG 41: 'the use of generative AI tools crosses the boundary of acceptable collaboration'; AI is not an acceptable collaborator, P96.

units.passage: Even when they convey a sense of authorial responsibility, AI tools produce statistically plausible word orderings without an intellectually or morally responsible author.
units.why: AI tools 'produce statistically plausible word orderings without an intellectually or morally responsible author', denying AI authorship; P96 fits.

units.passage: tools like Grammarly, ChatGPT, or Quillbot are aids, not authors.
units.why: The reminder 'tools like Grammarly, ChatGPT, or Quillbot are aids, not authors' says AI is not the author of submitted work, which matches P96 (AI as neither author nor collaborator).
units.fit_note: Also names Grammarly and Quillbot as aids, implying writing-support tools are acceptable aids.
